newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope is back at work after operation - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Pope is back at work after operation - spokesman.

text.p: Pope John Paul is back at work following an operation to remove his appendix last week and will resume his weekly general audience next Wednesday, the Vatican's chief spokesman said on Thursday.
"The Pope is well and immediately started to work again even though his doctors have advised him to rest," the spokesman, Joaquin Navarro-Valls, told Italy's Radio Dimensione Suono.
"The Pope will return to meeting pilgrims at his Wednesday general audience next week and will resume his Sunday visits to Rome parishes soon," Navarro-Valls said.

The Pope's doctors have said the 76-year-old Pontiff was recovering well from the October 15 appendectomy but had urged him to slow down. They said the operation confirmed that there was no recurrence of a colon tumour removed in 1992.
He was released from hospital on Tuesday after a 10-day stay. He appeared briefly at the window of his quarters overlooking the Vatican's St Peter's Square on Wednesday.
His next public appearance is due on Sunday, when he will recite his weekly prayer and address from the same window.
